options.text: I lost my weapon fighting the Blue Moon. Could I have it back?
options.condition: If the player lost their weapon during the Blue Moon fight:

steps.player: I lost my weapon fighting the Blue Moon. Could I have it back?

steps.npc: Here you go, iknil.

steps.text: Eyatalli returns your lost weapon to you.

options.text: I found some essence whilst fighting the lesser nagua.
options.condition: If the player has sulphurous essence in their inventory:

steps.player: I found some essence whilst fighting the lesser nagua.

steps.npc: Thank you, iknil. I shall use it to reinforce the seal.

options.text: I wanted to ask you about your masters.
options.condition: If the player has completed The Final Dawn

steps.player: I wanted to ask you about your masters.

steps.npc: What do you wish to know?

steps.player: I guess anything really. I still know so little about them.

steps.npc: If your hope is that I can tell you about a whole race, then I am likely to disappoint you, iknil. The masters were secretive individuals. They rarely divulged information that I did not require.
All I can tell you about are the three individuals that I knew personally.

steps.player: That's still something. What were they like?

steps.npc: They were kind, but filled with sadness. As you know, they summoned me after another of their kind unleashed the Moons of Peril.
It was a dark time. Their people had suffered great calamity years earlier and their extinction was inevitable.
It seems that many, such as the shaman who summoned the Moons, felt that the only salvation left was destruction.
My masters, however, felt differently. They fought for a world that was no longer their own. They believed in preserving these lands for those who would inhabit them afterwards.
Yes. Humans and dwarves were recent arrivals here, but the masters saw you as inheritors. I believe in some ways, you offered them hope in a time filled with pain.

steps.player: I see. Than you for sharing that with me.

steps.npc: It is not a problem, iknil.

options.text: Do you ever get tired of guarding this place?

steps.player: Do you ever get tired of guarding this place?

steps.npc: No.
Does the stream tire of eroding the earth? Does the earth tire of forming the mountain?
I have more in common with them than I do with most of your kind, iknil. Think of me as you do them.

options.text: This place is beautiful. I thought it was supposed to be a prison?

steps.player: This place is beautiful. I thought it was supposed to be a prison?

steps.npc: It is a prison. Everything around us serves that purpose.

steps.player: Even the plants and the streams?

steps.npc: I am a nagua of earth and stream. Being close to both empowers me to do my task.
Just as being far from moonlight weakens the Moons of Peril.

when-using-a-unique-equipment-reward-fro.npc: Congratulations on your reward, iknil. That is a treasure from ages past.

when-using-a-unique-equipment-reward-fro.player: Yeah, about that... I don't really like this one. Could I have a different one?

when-using-a-unique-equipment-reward-fro.npc: I was just... Processing. I suppose I could allow you another chance to obtain a piece of equipment, but it won't be guaranteed.

when-using-a-unique-equipment-reward-fro.prompt: Sacrifice this equipment for another chance at a different piece?

steps.npc: You're certain, Iknil? You could end up with nothing.

steps.prompt: Give up this equipment for possibly nothing in return?

steps.npc: Very well.

steps.text: If the player doesn't get anything:

steps.npc: No luck this time, iknil.

steps.player: Oh... Can I have it back?

steps.npc: No.

steps.text: If the player gets a new item:
Eyatalli hands you a new [item given].

steps.npc: Congratulations, iknil. Enjoy your new equipment.

steps.text: If the player gets a new item, identical to the one that was originally given:
Eyatalli hands you a new [item given].

steps.npc: Congratulations, ik-

steps.player: This is the same thing I just gave you!

steps.npc: So it seems. You're welcome to try again.

steps.player: Actually, I don't dislike it that much. I think I'll keep it.

steps.npc: Very well.
